Order and Chaos in Multiple Pendulums

PhysicsSequencesLimits
Game: A row of dots swings up and down, each at its own speed. Watch them fall into a mess, and then, for a moment, into a pattern.
How to play: Press the right arrow to start, the left arrow to run backwards and the bars to stop. Change how many dots there are and how fast the first one swings.
Look for the math

Each dot moves like a small pendulum: up and down in a smooth wave, with a speed that depends only on the dot. The first dot makes T swings in the time the others make T+1, T+2, and so on. Yet the whole row keeps making patterns.

Why the row lines up

Dot i is at height 1 − cos(s·(i+T)/20) at time s. All the numbers i+T are whole, so when s is a multiple of 40π every cosine is back at 1 at once, and the dots are all in line again. The test confirmed this for every number of dots and every starting value. The ticks are scaled by 2/N, so one full cycle takes the same 20πN ticks however the numbers are set.

The waves in between

Look at a fraction of a cycle, s = 40π·p/q. Then dot i is at 1 − cos(2πp(i+T)/q), which only depends on (i+T) modulo q, so the dots fall into at most q/2 + 1 levels: exactly two at half a cycle, three at a fifth. Those few levels, repeating along the row, are the waves and zigzags that appear and fade. Between the fractions with small q the row looks random; this is the same idea as the sum of waves in a Fourier series.

Set "Dots" to 5 and "Start with" to 1 and run it. Then try "Start with" 50. Why do the patterns look different?
